content.value_statement: Scaling cocktail batches can introduce unit errors, unsuitable rounding, and hidden assumptions. This skill produces a reconciled ingredient sheet with explicit tolerances, manual actions, and optional container fit.
actual_capabilities: Calculates one scale factor from original and target yields that share the same unit.
Applies linear, upward count, and manual review modes to every recipe line.
Rounds measured ingredients to supplied increments using nearest, upward, or downward policies.
Reports percentage deviation and blocks results outside the user-defined tolerance.
Calculates container count and unused capacity when matching capacity data is supplied.
Preserves manual actions separately and produces an explicit readiness status.
limitations: It does not convert units; original, target, and container yield units must match.
It does not add dilution, prep loss, carbonation behavior, storage guidance, or sensory validation.
It requires explicit rounding increments, tolerance, and scaling modes for every ingredient.
It processes one normalized recipe per calculation and depends on local Python 3 execution.

use_cases.title: Scale a service batch
use_cases.description: Expand a single cocktail into a measured service batch while keeping garnishes, rinses, and other manual actions visible.

use_cases.title: Plan drinks for guests
use_cases.description: Convert a known recipe to a chosen serving count with clear ingredient rounding and tolerance checks.

use_cases.title: Check container requirements
use_cases.description: Calculate required container count and unused capacity for a target liquid yield.

prompt_templates.title: Scale by servings
prompt_templates.prompt: Scale this cocktail from [original servings] to [target servings]. Ingredients: [list]. Use [tolerance]% and show every rounding decision.

prompt_templates.title: Preserve manual actions
prompt_templates.prompt: Scale this recipe to [target servings]. Treat [garnish, rinse, spray, or top-up] as manual and explain each preserved action.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a container batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Scale [original yield and unit] to [target yield and unit]. Use a [capacity and unit] container and report unused capacity.

prompt_templates.title: Audit rounding and tolerance
prompt_templates.prompt: Scale this recipe using the supplied mode and increment for each line. Report raw amounts, rounded amounts, deviations, blockers, and readiness.

output_examples.input: Scale one serving to eight with exact quarter-ounce and whole-piece increments. Use 1% tolerance and preserve the absinthe rinse.
output: Gin: 2 oz becomes 16 oz; lemon juice: 0.75 oz becomes 6 oz; peel: 1 becomes 8.
Absinthe rinse: manual per glass. Review state: READY FOR RECIPE REVIEW.

output_examples.input: Scale a 90 ml recipe to 750 ml with 5 ml increments, 3% tolerance, and a 500 ml container.
output: Spirit: 60 ml becomes 500 ml; vermouth: 30 ml becomes 250 ml.
Container fit: 2 containers with 250 ml unused capacity. Review state: READY FOR RECIPE REVIEW.

output_examples.input: Scale a two-serving recipe to 500 ml without an approved conversion or rounding policy.
output_examples.output: Review state: NOT READY: ROUNDING OR INPUT BLOCKER. Supply matching yield units, approved conversion data, rounding increments, and a tolerance.

best_practices: Use identical units for original yield, target yield, and container capacity.
Define a rounding increment and tolerance before running the calculation.
Review every manual line and every tolerance blocker before approving the recipe.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to infer conversions between servings and liquid volume.
Do not treat dilution, prep loss, garnishes, or process-sensitive steps as linear without a validated rule.
Do not omit rounding policies and then accept an apparently precise result.

faq.question: Can this skill convert ounces to milliliters?
faq.answer: No. Supply original and target yields in the same unit, or provide an approved conversion before scaling.

faq.question: Does it calculate cocktail dilution?
faq.answer: No. Dilution remains outside the calculation unless you provide a validated numeric rule for a separate recipe line.

faq.question: How are garnishes and rinses handled?
faq.answer: They can remain manual actions with notes, so they do not enter the numeric ingredient total.

faq.question: What happens when rounding exceeds tolerance?
faq.answer: The affected ingredient becomes a blocker, and the result is marked not ready for recipe review.

faq.question: Can it calculate container needs?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide capacity in the target yield unit to receive container count and unused capacity.

faq.question: Does the skill verify taste or physical stability?
faq.answer: No. It verifies arithmetic and declared rounding rules, but sensory quality and physical behavior require human validation.
